title: Finding capture with context envelope (foundational)
description: Signature original: A useful finding is stored together with its context envelope: the task that produced it, the sources behind it, and a timestamp. The envelope is what makes a memory reusable later, because a bare fact without provenance cannot be trusted or refreshed. Captures are small by design; the archive holds the full records, memory holds the distilled findings. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

t: Retention policy with TTL and pinning (foundational)
title: Retention policy with TTL and pinning (foundational)
description: Signature original: Every memory carries a time-to-live and a pin flag. Unpinned memories expire when their TTL lapses; pinned ones survive until explicitly unpinned, which protects hard-won findings from routine cleanup. TTLs are set by finding type: volatile operational notes get days, durable reference facts get years. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
from datetime import date, timedelta
mem = {'a': {'ttl_days': 7, 'pinned': False, 'born': date(2026, 10, 10)},
       'b': {'ttl_days': 7, 'pinned': True, 'born': date(2026, 10, 1)}}
today = date(2026, 10, 21)
for k, m in mem.items():
    alive = m['pinned'] or (today - m['born']).days <= m['ttl_days']
    print(k, 'alive' if alive else 'expired')

title: Memory indexing by topic signature (foundational)
description: Signature original: Memories are indexed by a topic signature: the set of significant terms in the finding, minus stopwords. Lookup intersects the query's terms with the index, which is fast and needs no vector machinery for moderate memory sizes. The signature doubles as a deduplication key: a new finding with an identical signature to an existing one updates it instead of duplicating it. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).

t: Recall ranking by recency and reuse (foundational)
title: Recall ranking by recency and reuse (foundational)
description: Signature original: When several memories match, they are ranked by a score combining recency, past reuse count, and source reliability. Frequently reused findings float up because reuse is evidence of value; stale, never-reused ones sink. The ranking is deliberately simple so its behavior stays explainable to the user. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
cands = [('m1', 2, 12, 0.9), ('m2', 30, 1, 0.9), ('m3', 5, 8, 0.4)]  # id, age_days, reuses, reliability
ranked = sorted(cands, key=lambda m: (m[2] * m[3]) / (1 + m[1]), reverse=True)
print('recall order:', [m[0] for m in ranked])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Persistent Knowledge Memory, 2026-10-21.

title: Expiry sweep with audit trail (foundational)
description: Signature original: A scheduled sweep removes expired, unpinned memories and writes each removal to an audit trail with the reason. Nothing is deleted silently: the trail records what was forgotten and why, so a user can see that a memory aged out rather than vanished mysteriously. Sweeps run frequently enough that the store never accumulates dead weight. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
from datetime import date
store = {'old': {'born': date(2026, 9, 1), 'ttl': 30, 'pinned': False},
         'new': {'born': date(2026, 10, 20), 'ttl': 30, 'pinned': False}}
trail = []
today = date(2026, 10, 21)
for k in list(store):
    m = store[k]
    if not m['pinned'] and (today - m['born']).days > m['ttl']:
        trail.append((k, 'expired TTL')); del store[k]
print('remaining:', list(store), '| trail:', trail)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Persistent Knowledge Memory, 2026-10-21.
